reading.body:
Voice and audio AI tools split almost evenly between speech processing and sound generation, but the sharpest risk pattern in this data concerns identity: at least six tools involve voice cloning or synthesis with explicit notes about likeness rights and consent requirements.

The consent signal is not incidental. Tools from Descript, ElevenLabs, Lovo, Resemble AI, and Respeecher all carry notes about likeness or consent risk, and Descript specifically records consent as a product step. Udio carries an active litigation flag. That concentration of legal exposure in a single capability, voice replication, suggests the category's near-term regulatory pressure will land there first, not on transcription or enhancement.

Jurisdictional spread is modest but real. Vendors operate out of the US, UK, Luxembourg, Spain, Ukraine, India, and Japan. That matters for GDPR applicability, for data residency choices in enterprise procurement, and for the governing law of any likeness dispute. Soundraw's Japan entry notes JASRAC considerations specifically, which is the only instance in this data of a named collecting society appearing as a compliance variable. What the data does not cover is compute footprint, infrastructure hosting arrangements, or the power demand behind any of these services, so no inference about grid load or scaling constraints is warranted here.
